facts.text: Kickapoo Site 6 sits in southwestern Brown County, within the western part of the Kickapoo Reservation.
Site 6 emerged as a parcel amid federal allotment processes that reduced the tribal land base by over 90% from its original bounds.
The Kickapoo people began as an Algonquian‑speaking Woodland tribe in the Great Lakes region, farming corn, beans, and squash while hunting and gathering.
The area has a humid continental climate, averaging 53.3°F annually, with hot summers and brief, severe winter cold spells.
Tallgrass prairie once dominated the landscape, but much has become cropland; remaining riparian zones and wetlands support diverse plant communities.
The name Kickapoo comes from words meaning 'he stands about' or 'he moves about standing here and there,' hinting at a semi‑nomadic past.
